Question_text: Hydrated sodium carbonate is sometimes known as washing soda. An aqueous solution of washing soda, P, is made by dissolving 13.73g of washing soda crystals in water to make 200 cm³ of solution. The mass of sodium carbonate, Na2CO3, in this aqueous solution of washing soda is determined by titration with dilute nitric acid, HNO3(aq). Na2CO3 + 2HNO3 → 2NaNO3 + CO2 + H2O Methyl orange is used to determine the end-point of the titration. Q is 0.400mol/dm³ HNO3(aq). (a) Fill the burette with Q. Pipette 25.0cm³ of P into a flask and titrate with Q using three drops of methyl orange as the indicator. The end-point is the first appearance of a pink colour that remains for 30 seconds. Record your results in the table. Repeat the titration as many times as necessary to achieve consistent results.
